# Three Organs, Three Jobs

<!-- STEP id="divide-the-work" -->
## Too Much Power in One Place

The danger is too much power in one place, so the work is divided among three organs of government:

- The **legislature** makes laws.
- The **executive** implements them, or puts them into action.
- The **judiciary** interprets them, or says what they mean.

<!-- STEP id="specialists-watching" -->
## One Law, Three Organs

Follow one law, a rule that every scooter rider must wear a helmet. Parliament passes it, and the police carry it out on the road.

A rider who is fined and thinks the fine is wrong can go to a court, and the court decides what the law means in that case.

<!-- STEP id="no-concentration" -->
## Separation of Powers

This is called **separation of powers**: each organ has distinct responsibilities, so each can do its own work well.

**Separation of powers prevents the concentration of power in any one organ.**

Three separate organs could still each make mistakes, so something must keep them in check. We look at that next.
